question.text: Can the holders of the quota rights organize to lobby for keeping or tightening the cap at a cost below their stake?

answer.rationale: Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-054 (illustrative figures), A-3: holders expect slots to last past the 2032 review without reallocation.

question.text: Do holders and buyers of the licenses or quota rights expect the restriction to last for many years?

answer.rationale: Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-054 (illustrative figures), A-10: airlines differ in the value they get from a WXI slot.

question.text: Do holders of the rights differ in their costs, or in the value they get from the right?

answer.rationale: Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-054 (illustrative figures), A-4: a slot market forms; slots are sold, leased and retimed at low transaction cost.

question.text: Can the rights be sold or leased at low cost (a register, few restrictions on who may hold them)?

answer.rationale: Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-054 (illustrative figures), A-5: airlines expected base-season history to set their share (the draft named the base seasons) and some could add off-peak daytime movements at a cost below the expected value of the extra slots.

question.text: During the base period, will actors know (or expect) that rights will be allocated by their activity in it?

source_sentences: Curfew (K1), a prohibition of takeoffs and landings from 23:00 to 06:00.
It binds all operators at WXI, with no movements permitted, subject to U1.
Emergencies, medical and state flights are exempt.
Enforcement is by the WAA, from air traffic control's movement log.
The penalties are $50,000 per movement in the curfew without a dispensation and $10,000 per daytime movement without a slot; slots of a holder fined three times in a season may be withdrawn.
Movements from 06:00 to 23:00 are capped at 380 a day (the summer 2025 scheduled number), binding all operators at WXI; the existing hourly limit of 34 stays.
Slots may be sold or leased, and retimed to another daytime hour where the hourly limit leaves room.

The 380 daily slots are issued free to airlines in proportion to the daytime movements each operated in the summer 2026 and winter 2026/27 seasons, each slot in the hour of the movement that earned it.
The WAA board published the draft order, including the base seasons, on 2 March 2026, after a residents' campaign for a curfew that had run since 2023.
Slots are issued on 1 September 2027; the curfew and the cap take effect with the winter season on 31 October 2027. No expiry; the WAA will review the cap in 2032.
Enforcement is by the WAA, from air traffic control's movement log.
The penalties are $50,000 per movement in the curfew without a dispensation and $10,000 per daytime movement without a slot; slots of a holder fined three times in a season may be withdrawn.
Fourteen airlines operate in the daytime; the three largest operate about 60% of daytime movements.
Allocation by history (K3), a rights allocation.

The 380 daily slots are issued free to airlines in proportion to the daytime movements each operated in the summer 2026 and winter 2026/27 seasons, each slot in the hour of the movement that earned it.

Slots of a holder that ceases to operate at WXI, or that uses a slot on fewer than 80% of a season's days, return to the WAA and are reissued free, first to night operators (those with night movements in winter 2026/27) in proportion to their night movements, then to new entrants.

context: In the summer 2025 season WXI handled about 420 movements (a takeoff or a landing) a day: about 380 between 06:00 and 23:00, and about 40 between 23:00 and 06:00.
The runway's declared capacity is 34 movements an hour (an existing rule, set by the WAA from air traffic control's assessment)
Daytime movements have grown about 3% a year and night cargo about 5%.
Pellham Regional Airport, 70 km away by motorway (about 55 minutes), is run by a separate authority, has no curfew, and uses about 45% of its runway capacity.
Overnight parcel delivery is sold in a national market; Wexcombe's region is about 4% of it.
The WAA's charges (about $2,000 per movement on average, about $13 per seat) are set each year to recover its costs, which are mostly fixed.

readings: U1-a: a flight scheduled before 23:00 and delayed may land or take off until 00:00, as of right
U1-b: there is no dispensation for ordinary delays; after 23:00 only emergencies operate, and a late flight diverts (in practice to Pellham) or is cancelled
unclear.text: Late-running flights: whether a flight scheduled before 23:00 and delayed may operate until 00:00 as of right, or has no dispensation for ordinary delays.
